results.1:

The rest is unchanged, so coder.settings and reviewer.settings, which both point at *d, now resolve to sonnet too.
results.2: Same as route 1 (all five arms): exit 0, the same one-line change, and the aliases now resolve to sonnet. It was not refused, even though the values behind the aliases changed.

context.in_practice: In this run the two routes behaved exactly the same. Every edit succeeded with exit 0, no output and identical file contents, and no refusal (exit 3) happened. The difference only shows up if a rewrite goes wrong. Route 1 checks just the value you set, so a stray change elsewhere in the file would still be written. Route 2 reloads the whole config, includes and aliases included, and refuses with no write if anything else changed. Even so, route 2 accepted `defaults.model`, whose change carries through the aliases, so its "nothing else changes" rule must count alias effects as expected.
context.stakes: Every `config set` is checked before it writes. A strict check refuses edits that would quietly change something besides the target, and a loose check might let a bad rewrite reach disk. In this run, all five edits passed the check and were written the same way on both routes.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 is a simple check that only catches problems at the path you set; route 2 also catches damage elsewhere in the config but needs a growing list of allowances (include conversion, aliases, schema) to avoid refusing legitimate edits.

plan_why: Five sets whose edits are prone to renderer errors or meant to change more than PATH: an anchor edit that must also change its alias, an alias expansion, converting a scalar include to an override, a quoted append to a flow list, and a multi-line append below a trailing comment. Each one shows whether the implementation writes the file, refuses with exit 3, or writes text that no longer reads back correctly.
routes: Re-parse the edited text and compare only the value at PATH with VALUE
Reload the whole configuration from the edited in-memory texts; require PATH to read back as VALUE and nothing else to change; otherwise exit 3 with no write
